newsitem.title: CHINA: Coca-Cola opens 18th China bottling plant.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola opens 18th China bottling plant.

text.p: U.S. soft-drinks giant Coca-Cola Co has opened its 18th bottling plant in China in northeastern Heilongjiang province, company officials said on Tuesday.

The $22 million plant in the provincial capital of Harbin was jointly owned by Kerry Beverages with 60 percent of the stock and the Harbin Economic and Technological Zone Industrial Development Co with 25 percent, Coca-Cola said in a statement.
China's National Cereals, Oil and Foodstuffs Import-Export Corp owned the remaining 15 percent of the bottling plant, it said.
The plant was the sixth of 10 Coca-Cola bottling ventures run by Kerry Beverages, a joint venture between Coca-Cola Co and Malaysian tycoon Robert Kuok's Kerry Holdings, it said.
Coca-Cola would have 23 bottling plants in China by 1997, bringing total investment to $500 million, it said, but gave no further details.
